free_tier.stated: The free tier still exists and the pricing page still prints 'Free of charge' against input and output for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Flash-Lite and other models, and against context caching for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash (2.5 Flash-Lite caching reads 'Not available'), but Google has stopped publishing how much the free tier carries. The rate-limits page now says only 'Rate limits depend on a variety of factors (such as your usage tier) and can be viewed in Google AI Studio', and the per-model free table the page carried through 2025 has been removed. The free columns that remain describe what is free, never how much. A Google AI Developers Forum post dated 2026-09-03 quotes 20 RPD on Gemini 3.8 Flash against 500 RPD on Flash-Lite.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: the pricing page lists the Batch API (50% cost reduction) under the Paid plan; its Free Tier Batch rows read 'Not available' for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash and 2.5 Flash-Lite, but 'Free of charge' for input and output on Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and 3.1 Flash-Lite. The rate-limits page publishes Batch enqueued-token quotas for Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 only, so a batch on the Flash models needs a billing account, and the free Flash-Lite batch path has no published quota.

limits.value: requests per day binds, not tokens: at a reported 20 RPD on Gemini 3.8 Flash the monthly ceiling is 600 requests, so a 1,000-item job at three requests an item never completes on one free project.

notes: Arithmetic, labelled estimate: 20 RPD x 30 days = 600 requests a month per model. The gap is the finding: a reader who trusts the word 'generous' on the pricing page and not the forum will design a batch that cannot run. Not measured: limits appear only in AI Studio after an account exists, so the 20 RPD figure rests on a forum report, and the 2025 archive's 250 RPD for 2.5 Flash disagrees with it by an order of magnitude.
